goal: Atomically cut the repository over to the Styio IDE and Coding Agent product roots with no legacy source or compatibility layer left behind.
description: Scope: repository product roots, package metadata, imports, scripts, CI, packaging, current product documentation, and the one-time removal proof. Context: one Flutter package currently owns IDE and Agent implementation while duplicate export facades preserve older layouts; splitting this over several green commits would require the compatibility implementation that the target architecture forbids. Target: products/styio_ide and products/styio_coding_agent are independently analyzable packages, packages/styio_agent_protocol is a pure typed boundary, Styio IDE launches without an Agent, repository tooling points only at final roots, and frontend/vityo_app plus duplicate facades are deleted in the same closure. Design Considerations: use one mechanical import/package rewrite followed by compile-guided fixes; keep current behavior while separating ownership; create the permanent resolved-dependency boundary gate and a temporary removal report. Design Value: every later lifecycle starts from an honest two-line repository instead of adding another organizational layer. Constraints & Risks: this is the only cross-line implementation lifecycle; do not retain deprecated exports, dual reads, copied implementations, or a second cleanup phase.

decisions.composition: One atomic cutover creates final product roots, a neutral protocol, and a thin IDE composition root.
decisions.algorithms: A deterministic import/package rewrite is followed by resolved dependency analysis and compile-guided repairs.
decisions.data_structures: Package dependency graphs and import edges are normalized sets keyed by canonical repository-relative paths.
decisions.state: After cutover there is one owner for each implementation and no compatibility state.
decisions.isolation: The permanent gate forbids IDE-to-Agent implementation imports, Agent-to-IDE imports, and Flutter in the Agent product.
decisions.concurrency: The migration is serialized as one commit boundary; parallel product work begins only after it closes.

acceptance_criteria.text: The final IDE, Coding Agent, and protocol packages analyze and smoke-test from their target roots, and Styio IDE starts with no Agent process installed.
The permanent product-line boundary gate passes and the one-time removal report finds no active old package/import/root, duplicate Agent implementation, or compatibility export.

goal: Make Styio IDE independently useful and establish revisioned workspace transactions as the only authority for Agent-originated edits.
description: Scope: products/styio_ide IDE editor/workspace domain, standalone composition, transaction previews, conflict detection, and focused tests. Context: current Agent context and patch application reach concrete editor/workspace types, so the future process boundary needs a narrow revisioned host contract rather than serialized copies of controllers. Target: the IDE opens and edits without an Agent; document and workspace revisions are monotonic; snapshots carry provenance; proposed edits bind to base revisions and can be previewed, accepted, rejected, conflicted, rolled back, and receipted; no Agent-facing path writes files directly. Design Considerations: preserve the existing source-buffer and transaction engine where correct, use immutable change sets and a serialized commit lane, and expose only host DTOs. Design Value: truthful collaboration depends on a single edit authority and deterministic conflict semantics. Constraints & Risks: do not redesign the editor rendering engine or add an Agent dependency; stale edits must fail without partial mutation.

interfaces.name: WorkspaceTransactionService
interfaces.outputs: preview, conflict facts, commit or rollback receipt
errors: commit failure with no partial application

decisions.composition: Existing editor buffers feed one workspace revision and transaction service behind host-facing DTOs.
decisions.algorithms: Edits are sorted and range-validated before a serialized atomic commit; stale revisions fail before mutation.
decisions.data_structures: Immutable resource-to-edit maps, monotonic revision counters, and interval checks represent change sets.
decisions.state: Document stores own text; the transaction service owns preview and commit lifecycle; presentation owns neither.
decisions.isolation: Agent-originated edits use the same preview/commit path as other workspace edits and cannot reach filesystem adapters directly.
decisions.concurrency: Reads may run concurrently; commits serialize per workspace and publish one revision after success.

acceptance_criteria.text: Styio IDE opens, edits, saves, searches, and closes a workspace with every Agent capability disabled or absent.
Revisioned transaction tests prove preview, commit, reject, conflict, rollback, and zero partial mutation for stale or failed Agent change sets.

goal: Close the truthful Styio IDE developer loop and expose the same revision-bound facts to users and Agent clients.
description: Scope: IDE language, execution, testing, debugging, source control, terminal, toolchain, package, capability, and receipt services plus one representative product fixture. Context: many current surfaces and adapters exist, but partial or unavailable routes are mixed with large context snapshots and the old plan treats AI as a separate provider feature. Target: every developer operation returns versioned facts or a structured available/degraded/blocked result; a real fixture completes edit-save-analyze-test-run; Agent-facing fact providers reuse these sources and carry revision/provenance rather than copying presentation state. Design Considerations: retain adapter boundaries for compiler/process/SCM seams, normalize capability and receipt envelopes, and invalidate facts by revision/event rather than polling full state. Design Value: an Agent can only be trustworthy when it observes the same factual developer loop the user sees. Constraints & Risks: do not reimplement compiler semantics, infer success, or make upstream availability a hidden skip.

Every unavailable or heuristic route tested by the suite reports an explicit degraded/blocked state, and Agent-facing facts match the user-facing source revision.

goal: Implement Styio IDE as a supervised, concurrent, ACP-compatible Agent Client with a versioned neutral protocol.
description: Scope: shared protocol schemas/DTOs, IDE Agent Client registry, stdio transport, process supervisor, session reducers, capability negotiation, permissions, cancellation, reconnect, and conformance fixtures. Context: the current app constructs and calls Agent controllers in process; a true Agent Client must host independent runtimes and remain stable when they fail. Target: Styio IDE launches or attaches compatible Agents, serves several correlated sessions, streams bounded events, performs bidirectional requests, handles dynamic capabilities, and fails closed on invalid versions/messages; Styio extensions are negotiated and namespaced. Design Considerations: model ACP core semantics directly, keep transport separate from session state, use one serialized reducer per session, and generate/validate DTOs from canonical schema. Design Value: an open process boundary makes Styio Coding Agent independently testable and lets other compatible Agents participate. Constraints & Risks: never serialize editor controllers or credentials; cap message/event sizes; process termination must verify no orphan.

interfaces.name: AgentClientTransport
interfaces.inputs: versioned JSON-RPC requests, responses, notifications, and cancellation
interfaces.outputs: correlated bounded message stream and process lifecycle receipts

dependencies.reason: Canonical schemas are the source for validated DTOs and compatibility fixtures.
The IDE consumes neutral messages rather than Agent runtime types.

decisions.composition: A registry supervises transports; each session has one reducer and immutable projection.
decisions.algorithms: Correlation maps route responses/events in constant expected time; bounded queues apply backpressure.
decisions.data_structures: Maps keyed by Agent/session/request ID, immutable capability sets, and bounded deques hold hot events.
decisions.state: Process, transport, session, and permission state machines have distinct owners.
decisions.isolation: Agents run out of process with minimal environment and cannot access IDE objects.
decisions.concurrency: Sessions run concurrently; events within one session reduce serially; cancellation is correlated and idempotent.

acceptance_criteria.text: Protocol and process tests prove negotiation, streaming, concurrent sessions, bidirectional permission requests, cancellation, reconnect, and orphan-free shutdown.
Unsupported versions, malformed/oversized messages, revoked capabilities, and failed processes produce bounded structured failures without affecting editor state or sibling sessions.

goal: Deliver the AI-native Styio collaboration workbench for concurrent tasks, visible control, and reviewable changes.
description: Scope: IDE collaboration store and presentation surfaces for task/thread lists, turns, plans, steps, tool activity, permissions, artifacts, diagnostics, diffs, receipts, steering, cancellation, retry, and reconnect. Context: the current Agent surface is a bottom-panel singleton wired to one concrete controller, so work disappears into UI state and cannot represent independent sessions. Target: users can run and inspect at least two sessions, route input/permissions to the right session, leave the panel without losing pending work, review change sets against base revisions, and apply or reject through the workspace transaction service. Design Considerations: normalize protocol events into immutable ID-keyed state, virtualize long lists, retain bounded hot windows, and keep pending attention visible in the workbench/task center. Design Value: this is the user-visible collaboration model that distinguishes an Agent-native IDE from a chat feature. Constraints & Risks: no hidden auto-apply, no widget-owned durable truth, and no cross-session mutable list.

decisions.concurrency: Independent sessions update concurrently while each session projection reduces in order.

A proposed multi-file change is reviewed by file/hunk and then accepted, rejected, conflicted, or reverted only through the authoritative workspace transaction path.

goal: Expose bounded IDE context and tools through narrow native interfaces and an MCP-compatible, root-safe host.
description: Scope: IDE native tool adapters, MCP server, resource/prompt providers, root registry, capability discovery, revision/provenance envelopes, extension contributions, redaction, limits, and conformance tests. Context: publishing every command or serializing the current giant Agent context would create an unsafe, expensive API; official IDE/MCP designs distinguish deep native tools from reusable external tools. Target: compatible Agents discover only task-relevant tools/resources/prompts and approved roots; roots and capabilities can change during a session; every result is revisioned, bounded, redacted, and typed; removed access is denied immediately. Design Considerations: wrap existing IDE services with narrow host adapters, use lazy providers and stable digests, canonicalize paths before root checks, and keep schemas versioned. Design Value: Agents gain real IDE leverage without importing implementation or receiving ambient machine access. Constraints & Risks: tool annotations are never enforcement; prevent traversal, symlink escape, secret/token passthrough, output flooding, and stale capability caches.

decisions.algorithms: Canonical path resolution precedes root containment; context candidates are lazily paged, deduplicated, and budget-packed.
decisions.data_structures: Immutable tool descriptor maps, root sets by session, content-digest dedupe sets, and bounded result pages.
decisions.state: Root/capability registries own authorization state; context providers own source caches; transport owns none.

decisions.concurrency: Discovery snapshots are immutable; root updates atomically replace a session set and invalidate affected requests.

Root traversal/symlink escape, revoked access, removed capabilities, oversized output, secret exposure, and token passthrough are denied and auditable.

goal: Harden Styio IDE collaboration for bounded performance, accessibility, recovery, failure isolation, and truthful desktop delivery.
description: Scope: IDE performance budgets, virtualized Agent surfaces, protocol/event backpressure, accessibility, session/process recovery, crash isolation, packaging, update metadata, and three desktop smoke lanes. Context: concurrent long-running Agents add event, diff, context, process, and notification pressure that a chat-oriented shell does not exercise. Target: large histories and diffs remain responsive and bounded; keyboard/screen-reader users can operate collaboration; IDE restarts recover task projections; a failed Agent affects neither editor nor siblings; Windows/macOS/Linux artifacts launch and report capabilities honestly. Design Considerations: measure before tuning, bound every hot buffer, virtualize by visible ranges, persist compact projections, and keep per-platform adapters behind one product contract. Design Value: AI-native collaboration is only credible if it remains controllable during long or failed tasks. Constraints & Risks: no dropped event may be silent; missing signing/host tooling is a failed or explicitly blocked platform result, not a green skip.

decisions.composition: Performance, accessibility, recovery, and packaging harden existing collaboration capabilities without a parallel UI.
decisions.algorithms: Visible-range virtualization, bounded queues, compact projection checkpoints, and supervised reconnect limit work.
decisions.data_structures: Ring buffers with dropped counters, indexed visible windows, and compact immutable recovery snapshots.
decisions.state: Each session persists a recoverable projection; platform packaging owns no runtime session state.
decisions.isolation: Agent process failures are contained per descriptor/session and platform adapters remain behind capability states.
decisions.concurrency: Backpressure is per session with global memory ceilings; shutdown/restart races are deterministically tested.

acceptance_criteria.text: Large-session performance, memory, backpressure, keyboard, screen-reader, restart, and Agent-failure-isolation tests meet documented budgets with explicit dropped/truncated counters.
Independent Windows, macOS, and Linux packaging smoke lanes launch Styio IDE on matching hosts, open a workspace, and report unavailable Agent/platform capabilities truthfully.

goal: Deliver a deterministic IDE full-suite orchestrator and fail-closed evidence receipt contract without executing the one-time full regression.

Context: Validation.md and the final-validation Node require ide/full, but scripts/styio_quality.py initially rejected that suite and could not record one outcome per REQ-IDE label. Target: provide a plan-only inspectable full-suite graph, atomic bounded JSON receipts, and current-source fingerprints while preserving the single later execution of the actual full suite. Design Considerations: compose existing focused commands without invoking Coding Agent full regression or consuming native package artifacts, reject duplicate or missing requirement mappings, and write receipts atomically. Design Value: the only full IDE run is executable and auditable while platform release lanes remain independent. Constraints & Risks: this Node must never execute ide/full; it validates the runner through plan-only and synthetic receipt fixtures, and the final-validation Node remains the sole authority to perform the real full run.

goal: Bind each native Styio IDE release receipt to its own source commit and fingerprint while keeping Windows, macOS, and Linux publication independent.
description: Closure: module - independent native desktop release lanes. Context: native packages can only be truthfully built and smoked on their matching hosts, so a shared three-platform commit gate is invalid. Target: retain bounded commit/fingerprint fields in each platform's smoke report, publish each artifact from its own matching-host lane, and keep ide/full platform-independent. Design Considerations: derive identity from the lane checkout, carry it as immutable input through the launched artifact, validate one lane at a time, and remove all cross-platform collection and join logic. Design Value: each platform can be submitted and released on its own truthful evidence. Constraints & Risks: no synthetic platform success, no environment or secret capture, no compatibility payload, no cross-platform collector, and no full IDE regression in this lifecycle.

Context: focused suites prove local closures but cannot prove the standalone IDE, concurrent collaboration, MCP boundary, recovery, and performance together. Target: execute Validation.md's ide/full suite once, record commit/platform/schema/fixture versions and an outcome per requirement, then sync and validate Better Plan state. Design Considerations: run the fixed suite without lowering targets, consuming native package artifacts, or rerunning Coding Agent's full suite; real IDE/Agent integration evidence may be consumed from the Agent line only when its content/version digest matches. Design Value: one auditable platform-neutral product result replaces accumulated partial claims while native releases remain independent. Constraints & Risks: a missing platform-independent fixture, required tool, or compatible Agent is a blocked/failing outcome; native host or signing availability is outside this gate.
